clue.text: Kipling's failed

parts.note: Kipling wrote a novel whose title says this thing failed, so the clue asks for the subject of that title

explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's novel The Light That Failed names this as the thing that failed.

clue.text: Possibly suit cruel poet?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way, so the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A question about whether some cruel lawsuit could be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns SUITCRUEL into the Roman poet's name; 'suit cruel' reads like a legal complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucretius was the Roman author of the didactic verse work De Rerum Natura.

clue.text: Novelist involved in Little King Igor

indicators.note: involved means twisted up together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a small k is the abbreviation for king, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A novelist mixed up in some business with a small monarch called Igor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' shuffles K and IGOR; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorki, also spelt Gorky, was the Russian writer of Mother.

clue.text: Conductor of opera feminist writer and I support

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits beneath the rest, so the I comes at the bottom of the entry

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera
Anaïs Nin, the diarist and writer of erotica admired by feminists

explanation.surface: A conductor of an opera is backed by a feminist writer and the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'support' means the pieces stand beneath one another, so I goes at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was the celebrated Italian orchestral and operatic maestro.

clue.text: Dramatist shows location of wheel on sailing vessel

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
a ship's wheel stands in the wheelhouse, so a house is where the wheel is

explanation.surface: The playwright reveals where the steering wheel sits on a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry, a piece written 'on' another follows it, so the order flips from the clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Brighouse was the Lancashire playwright of Hobson's Choice.

clue.text: Festival co-founder bitter on new composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A music festival founder writes a sour new piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' is the anagram signal on the sour word, and it also suits the musical surface; the Aldeburgh Festival is in Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten helped found the Aldeburgh Festival in Suffolk in 1948.

clue.text: English composer from another country

explanation.definitionFit: John Ireland was an English composer; Ireland is also a nation separate from England.

clue.text: He is south-eastern novelist

parts.note: taken as written
is shortens to 's
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-eastern

explanation.surface: A man described as coming from the south-east turns out to be a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Hesse was the German author of Steppenwolf and Siddhartha.

clue.text: Mann destroyed with IOU in America, everyone agrees

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for America

parts.note: US stands for the United States of America

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Thomas Mann's IOU torn up in the States, to universal approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' scrambles the novelist's name with the IOU, and 'in' tucks the result inside the abbreviation for America.
explanation.definitionFit: A unanimous decision is one where all parties are in full accord.

clue.text: Emma's comic writer

explanation.definitionFit: Mr Elton is the vicar in Jane Austen's Emma; Ben Elton is a British comedian and novelist.

clue.text: Erich isn't confused by Stephen King

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A man named Erich is bewildered by the horror writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen King's 1983 novel concerns a possessed car of that name.

clue.text: Snappy poet

explanation.definitionFit: Snappy dressing is stylish; Christopher Smart was the eighteenth-century poet of Jubilate Agno.

clue.text: Shaw's Galatea heard to be in pain in 1900

annotationWithheld.why: Shaw's Galatea heard to be in pain in 1900 (5): Eliza Doolittle is the definition, but no homophone of 'in pain' plus anything for 1900 yields the letters; the wordplay could not be confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Shaw's Galatea heard to be in pain in 1900

clue.text: His performance is headed for disaster at reading, unfortunately

definitions.text: His performance is headed for disaster

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An actor's show at the Reading theatre sadly heads for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges ATREADING; Reading is an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor in tragic roles performs plays that end in catastrophe.

clue.text: Like Jean Plaidy's woman or Iris Murdoch's girl

explanation.definitionFit: Plaidy wrote The Italian Woman and Murdoch wrote The Italian Girl, so both titles share this nationality.

clue.text: Location of Trollope's modest home

parts.note: modest stands for small, recalling a Trollope novel title naming the village where a little house stands

explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's novel The Small House at ... names this village.

clue.text: Runyon gambler in Motown

explanation.definitionFit: Nathan Detroit runs a crap game in Runyon-based Guys and Dolls; Motown is a nickname for the Michigan city.

clue.text: Scurrilous slave sits there, stirring it up

indicators.note: stirring things up means agitating, so the letters are churned around

explanation.surface: A foul-mouthed servant lounges about causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida calls this abusive Greek 'deformed and scurrilous'.

clue.text: Irish nationalist and US writer with manuscript collaborate in programme music

parts.note: Wolfe Tone led the 1798 United Irishmen rising
Edgar Allan Poe, the American storyteller

explanation.surface: An Irish rebel and an American author work together on a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral pieces depicting a story or scene are known as programme music.

clue.text: Activity associated with New York by Carol Ann Duffy

definitions.text: Activity associated with New York by Carol Ann Duffy

parts.words: Activity associated with New York by Carol Ann Duffy
parts.note: Duffy's poem title pairs a trading activity with Manhattan, the heart of New York

explanation.definitionFit: Duffy's collection and poem Selling Manhattan gives this commercial activity.

clue.text: "O'er whom Suwarrow shone like a — —" (Byron, Don Juan)

definitions.text: "O'er whom Suwarrow shone like a — —" (Byron, Don Juan)

parts.words: "O'er whom Suwarrow shone like a — —" (Byron, Don Juan)
parts.note: a quotation with two missing words from Byron's comic epic, describing the Russian general Suvorov at a siege

explanation.definitionFit: Byron likens General Suvorov's glow to a street light fuelled by coal vapour.

clue.text: His Nature was hard to fathom

definitions.text: His Nature was hard to fathom

parts.words: His Nature was hard to fathom
parts.note: Nature is the title of an essay by an American Transcendentalist, notorious for its difficulty, posing as a remark on character

explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson's 1836 essay Nature is famously dense.

clue.text: Cathedral town's Scot is delightful …

parts.note: Ely is a Cambridgeshire cathedral city, here in the possessive
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman from a cathedral town is a charming fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysian means blissful, like the Elysian Fields of Greek paradise.

clue.text: Abstract Expressionist featured in Read's work, and in Sky documentary

indicators.note: featured in says the painter appears within the run of words that follow

parts.words: Read's work, and in Sky documentary

explanation.surface: A painter appears in a book by Herbert Read and in a television documentary.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'worK AND IN SKY'; Herbert Read was a British art critic.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassily Kandinsky pioneered abstract art, a forerunner of Abstract Expressionism.

clue.text: … for a minute in dishevelled kilt, suggesting decadent avant garde painter

indicators.note: in places the minute's letter inside the mixed kilt
dishevelled means untidy, so the letters are tumbled

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A rumpled kilt hints at a fin-de-siècle Viennese artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishevelled' turns KILT into KLIT, and 'in' puts M inside it; the ellipsis links to 20 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Klimt led the Vienna Secession, known for opulent, sensual art.

clue.text: His supporters believe in ghosts

parts.note: reads as superstition but refers to fans of a Norwegian playwright's drama Ghosts

explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen wrote the play Ghosts, so his admirers champion it.

clue.text: Exclusive Waugh work

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper exclusive is a story others lack; Evelyn Waugh satirised journalism in his novel of that name.

clue.text: Alternative weight of dramatist

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A choice about the heaviness of a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Orton was the English playwright of Loot and Entertaining Mr Sloane.

clue.text: One beloved of Zeus gets thanks for tittles

parts.note: Io was a maiden loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer
ta is informal British for thank you, made plural here to match thanks

explanation.surface: A lover of the king of the gods receives gratitude for tiny marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tittle is a tiny jot, and an iota is likewise the smallest amount.

clue.text: French nobleman let out philosopher

parts.note: aristo is short for aristocrat, recalling the French nobles of the Revolution

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of let are mixed

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat is freed, and he proves to be a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aristo' is informal for aristocrat; 'let out' looks like a phrase meaning released, but 'out' is the anagram signal on 'let'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the Greek thinker who tutored Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Small part for viola

parts.note: reads as a minor role for a theatre character called Viola but means a small component used to adjust a stringed instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A small peg or pin on a stringed instrument is turned to adjust string pitch.

clue.text: Some of Blake's are more sophisticated than others

definitions.text: Some of Blake's are more sophisticated than others

parts.words: Some of Blake's are more sophisticated than others
parts.note: Blake wrote two linked verse collections, of Innocence and of Experience, so one set is worldlier

explanation.definitionFit: Blake's Songs of Experience are worldlier than his Songs of Innocence.
